## Establishment log (doubtful readings, misprints, other-print differences — the notes must say so)

# Establishment log — bardo-thodol-008 (pp. 72–79), 2026-11-22

Three readers on the strongest model checked the stored dzogchengonpa.org witness against the page images, line by line. Each
used crops at ×3, and ×5–×10 where a reading was in doubt. Reader A read pp. 72–74, B pp. 75–77 and C pp. 78–79. Each of
pp. 72–78 has five print lines. **p. 79 (leaf n80) has three lines and is the last page of text kha.** The next image, n82,
is the title leaf of text ga. The part therefore runs over pp. 72–79, not the pp. 72–80 that parts.json lists; the cite is
pp. 72–79. The witness's line breaks match the print on all 38 lines read. The leaf-front ornament ༄༅༔ ༔ is on pp. 73, 75,
77 and 79.

**Seam.** The part begins mid-line on 72.2 with དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་དེའི་ཤར་ནས…, right after bardo-thodol-007's
…ནམ་མཁའ་ལ་མཛད་པ་ཅིག་འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༔. Reader A's 72.1 and the start of 72.2 agree letter for letter with part 007.
**End.** The part ends at the end of text kha: …ཐོས་གྲོལ་ཆེན་མོ་ཐལ་ལོ༔ ཨྠྀི༔ རྒྱ་རྒྱ་རྒྱ༔ ༔.

The image overruled the witness 39 times: 18 for A, 14 for B and 7 for C. Full tables are in readings/read_A-log.md,
read_B-log.md and read_C-log.md. The main ones:
- Words: 72.3 འཛུམ, འཁྲིལ, ཐོད; 73.1 adds ལ; 73.2 བྱ; 73.3 adds འཆར; 73.5 ཁྲག; 74.2 adds the skipped དཔའ་བོ་དང་༔.
- Letters: 75.3 གཙོ; 76.3 འབྱུང; 77.1 བཅོམ; 77.2 གཏོད and དཔའ.
- 78.1 ལྕགས་ཀྱུས (the witness has སྐུས; the other recension agrees with the print).
- 78.1 the witness misplaces the tsheg in དུ་གསོལ and ཏུ་གཏོད; the print has them right.
- 79.3 འཕྲོད.

- 72.4 མདོག: the vowel stroke may be the tail of the letter above.
- 74.4 མི: an ink blot covers the vowel.
- 75.1 བྱེད: the first letter could be བ or ཕ. The other recension has ཕྱེད.

## `# fix:` lines (18)

Each was checked by script to apply exactly once.

**Line-join tshegs (10):** 72.3/4, 72.4/5, 74.2/3, 74.5/75.1 (across the ornament: འོང་ངོ༔ གརསྣ), 75.1/2, 76.3/4, 77.1/2,
77.3/4 and 78.2/3. The tenth is a mid-line tsheg the print lacks, at 73.4 ལྗང་ཁུསྐུ.

**Contractions written out (3):**
- 76.1 དེ་ཙན → དེ་ཙ་ན (the -n contraction of "therefore").
- 76.2 རང་སྒྲའབྲུག → རང་སྒྲ་འབྲུག.
- 77.5 the -གས ligature ལྕགྶ → ལྕགས.

**Misprints corrected (README rule 5b; the note must give the print's reading) (5):**
- 74.1 ཚོགས་དབག་ཏུ་མེད་པ → དཔག ("immeasurable"). The print itself has དཔག at 74.4.
- 74.1 རིགས་བཞིའི་མཁའ་གྲོ → མཁའ་འགྲོ. The letter is dropped; the phrase occurs four times in the same list.
- 75.5 དུད་འགྲེའི → དུད་འགྲོའི, as at 75.4, 76.4 and 76.5. The second o-stroke may only be worn away.
- 77.4 བདེ་གཤིགས → བདེ་གཤེགས (sugata).
- 77.5 ལྷ་ཚོཌ[?] → ལྷ་ཚོགས.

## Kept as printed, with a note

- 74.1 ཀྱི་རོལ་དུ: the other recension has ཕྱི་རིམ་དུ.
- 74.5 ཙམ་འདིར་བ་འོང: the other recension has ཙམ་དུ་ལྡིར་ནས.
- 77.2 and 78.1 མདུན་བརྩེ་གཅིག for འདུན་པ་རྩེ་གཅིག: twice, and parts 003 and 007 have མདུན་པ, so this is the print's habit.
- 77.5 ཨ་ཙ་མ་ར for the usual ཨ་ཙ་མ་རེ: nothing stands above the ར.
- 78.1 ཁོན་ནས: the other recension has ཁོ་ནར.
- 72.5 ལྡན་བ and 73.1 གཅིག for ཅིག: the print's own spelling.
- 79.3 **ཨྠྀི** is one stack: ཨ over a subjoined ཐ, with two gi-gu (ྀ + ི). It is the treasure-text closing *iti* "thus",
  written as one ligature, as Reader C reads it. pyewts gives `a+th-i+i`; the drafter needs a tib.py override for its
  letters and pronunciation.
- 79.3 རྒྱ་རྒྱ་རྒྱ༔ is the threefold seal.
- 79.3 དང༔ has no tsheg before the ༔.

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

The full list is in the reader logs, about 25 places. The main ones:
- 76.3 "comes with fierce terror" against "with fierce mantras".
- 76.5 སྐྱེས against ལྷུང ("be born" against "fall"), and བཀོལ་གཅོད against བཀོལ་སྤྱོད.
- 77.4 "held by compassion" against "by the rays of compassion".
- 78.3 ཚོགས་ཀྱི against རྣམས་ཀྱིས.
- 79.3 the print closes text kha with ཐལ་ལོ, the *iti* stack and the seals. The other recension has ལགས་སོ and runs straight on
  into the wrathful deities.

n79 carries the Arabic number 78, and n80 carries 79 and 80. n80 also has a Tibetan folio mark, read as སོ་དྲུག (36) followed by
one stack that could not be read. Leaf 36 fits text kha if its first leaf is p. 9.
